plugins.name: claude-code-notify
plugins.description:
claude-code-notify sends a desktop notification whenever Claude Code finishes responding, so you never miss a prompt while working across multiple sessions.

The plugin is focus-aware: if you're already looking at the Claude session (detected via tmux pane, window, and terminal focus state), the notification is suppressed.
On macOS without tmux, it checks whether your terminal app is frontmost.
A 5-second debounce prevents notification spam during rapid tool calls.

Works on Linux (notify-send) and macOS (osascript).
Requires jq and bash 4+.
tmux is optional but recommended for the best experience.

Configuration is zero-config by default, with two optional environment variables: CLAUDE_NOTIFY_CONTEXT (adds a Work/Personal prefix) and CLAUDE_NOTIFY_URGENCY (sets notification priority).

Includes /notify-help and /notify-test slash commands for easy setup verification.

Session-local metacognition harness for long-running Claude Code work.

When suggestions get reverted 3+ times within 10 tool calls, reflect invokes Opus 4.7 to reason about why the rejections clustered. The next turn auto-loads it via path-scoped rule injection and adjusts.

Key features:
• 3-tier weighted signal taxonomy: git revert/restore (Tier 1, +100), user-file deletes (Tier 2, +70), utterance negation regex (Tier 3, +50). Cumulative threshold 240 + 5-turn cooldown — fires only when reverts genuinely cluster.
• Single-shot Opus 4.7 with adaptive thinking (effort: high) and 3-layer prompt cache (L1 1h, L2 5m, L3 ephemeral).
Measured: cold ~$0.05, warm ~$0.01, 95.9% L1 cache hit.
• Two cross-platform hooks: PostToolUse (Tier 1+2) and UserPromptSubmit (Tier 3). Pure-bash arithmetic — no jq/bc dependency on Windows git-bash.
• Session-local by design: no persistence, no cross-session sync, no telemetry. The guidance file evaporates at session end.
• Failure modes characterized: cold-start refusal (< 5 turns), false-trigger flagging on intent shifts, abstention on regulatory/opaque domains.
• Optional localhost Next.js companion Viewer (binds 127.0.0.1, never deploys, PII redactor on every read) for live state + reflection history + cross-session drift clustering.
• MIT-licensed. SLSA v1 provenance via GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publisher (Sigstore-signed).

plugins.name: tidy

tidy provides an interactive TDD workflow powered by Kent Beck's Tidy First approach. You write a plan (a markdown checklist of small tasks), then execute them one by one through a strict Red → Green → Refactor cycle.

The plugin acts as a "Genie" — it executes your commands (go, refactor, commit) but never makes strategic decisions on its own. You stay in control of what to build, when to tidy, and when to commit.

Key features:

go: Write a failing test, then write the minimum code to pass it. One task at a time.
refactor: Apply one Tidy First pattern (Guard Clause, Extract Method, Rename, etc.) and verify tests still pass.
commit: Commit with strict separation — structural changes and behavioral changes never mix.
Built-in Tidy First patterns: 11 tidying patterns with prioritization (eliminate duplication → improve clarity → reduce complexity).
Context-constrained: Only loads the current task, never the full plan. Keeps the conversation focused.

The plugin covers four modes — full analysis, closet audit, single-item check, palette refinement — and honors genuine ambiguity with a between-seasons protocol instead of forcing binary verdicts. plugins.name: vanta-mcp-plugin

/vanta:fix-test <testId> — Generate an IaC fix and open a pull request for a specific failing test

plugins.name: vardoger
plugins.description:
vardoger personalizes Claude Code by analyzing your own conversation history and turning recurring patterns into tailored rules.

How it works: the plugin's `analyze` skill calls the `vardoger` CLI, which reads your local `~/.claude/projects/` session files in batches. Claude summarizes each batch for behavioral signals (tools you prefer, libraries you use, coding conventions you follow, mistakes you don't want repeated), then synthesizes the summaries into a single personalization that lands in your rules file. Re-running refreshes the personalization as your history grows.

Everything runs on your machine — conversations never leave your disk, there is no server or account, and the output is plain Markdown you can edit or delete. The same CLI also supports Cursor, Codex, and OpenClaw, so the personalization stays consistent across assistants if you use more than one.

Uses PreToolUse hooks to intercept manifest edits and install commands, blocking them until the developer verifies the latest version upstream.

plugins.name: versori-skills
plugins.description:
The versori-skills plugin gives Claude Code the ability to create, build, deploy, and monitor production-grade data integrations, entirely from the command line. Rather than stitching together simple automations, Versori enables Claude to build complex, multi-workflow integrations with full TypeScript control using the versori-run SDK.

The plugin follows a research-first approach: before writing any code, Claude gathers and structures API documentation for each system involved, producing a grounded research document that becomes the single source of truth for the integration. This ensures generated code is accurate and well-informed rather than hallucinated.

From there, Claude manages the full integration lifecycle: bootstrapping projects, configuring systems and connections, generating type-safe TypeScript workflows, running local validation via Deno, and deploying to production with built-in safety checks like dry-run previews and project context validation.

Key features:

- Research-grounded code generation: Claude researches API documentation before writing code, with every fact linked to its source. Research documents are uploaded as project assets so future modifications retain full context.
- Full project lifecycle management: Create, sync, deploy, version, promote, and rollback integrations without leaving the terminal. Supports multiple environments with version promotion between them.
- Complex multi-workflow integrations: Build integrations with scheduled ETL pipelines, webhook handlers, durable long-running workflows, and stateful batch processing using KV storage, going well beyond the simple trigger-action automations of platforms.
- Embedded integrations (multi-user): Supports user activations and connection management for embedded integration scenarios where end-users bring their own credentials.
- Secure credential handling: Credentials are referenced as environment variables and resolved at runtime. They are never embedded in commands or stored in code.
- Built-in deployment safety: Dry-run mode for all destructive operations.

plugins.name: vibe-doc
plugins.description: Vibe Doc is an AI-powered documentation gap analyzer for any codebase. It scans your project's artifacts, classifies the project type (web app, API, data pipeline, Claude Code plugin, etc.), measures coverage against a tier-appropriate documentation matrix, and either generates the missing docs from your existing artifacts or hands you a ranked list of gaps to close. Five slash commands cover the loop: /vibe-doc:scan (analyze), /vibe-doc:generate (write missing docs), /vibe-doc:check (CI deployment-readiness gate), /vibe-doc:status (snapshot), and /vibe-doc:evolve (Level-3 self-improvement — the plugin reads its own session logs and proposes SKILL improvements). Honest about coverage: no cherry-picked denominators, no false negatives the matcher has learned to flag.

plugins.name: vibe-iterate
plugins.description: Post-ship product iteration for Claude Code. Pick a banner mode — feature-add, competitive, ux-polish, or bug-bash — or reach for a sidecar (radar, spy, scan-releases, rate, ship, upgrade). Every run ships one PR, regression-aware and small-diff-preferred. The agent keeps an "Atlas" of what you've shipped, considered, and cut across sessions, and stays current on your stack via context7 plus a weekly framework-release scan. Composes with vibe-cartographer when it's installed; works standalone when it isn't. No telemetry — Atlas data stays local.

plugins.name: virtual-team
plugins.description:
Virtual Team turns Claude Code into a roster of 12 senior specialists you can summon by slash command. Instead of one generic assistant trying to be everything at once, you get focused expert mindsets — a backend engineer who actually thinks about input validation and authorization, a database engineer who asks about access patterns before suggesting indexes, a security engineer who threat-models the diff in front of them, a QA engineer who builds a test strategy before writing a single test. Each persona ships with a repeatable workflow and a
 structured output contract so the answers are scannable, prioritized, and actionable — not freeform prose you have to parse.

 The plugin is project-adaptive: every persona detects your stack (language, framework, package manager, conventions, existing patterns) at invocation time, so the same
 /virtual-team:frontend call gives sharp React advice in a React repo and sharp Svelte advice in a Svelte repo, with no per-project configuration. A shared review rubric and ecosystem context layer keeps recommendations grounded in real-world tradeoffs rather than textbook generalities.

Two meta-commands tie the roster together. /virtual-team:senior-brother is your generalist mentor — bring it anything, even a half-formed thought, and it figures out what you actually need, gives you the better solution, and tells you what you're lacking and how to level up. /virtual-team:all is the parallel orchestrator — point it at a PR or a feature and it
 dispatches every relevant specialist simultaneously, then synthesizes their findings into one prioritized report with a clear ship/hold verdict.

Who it's for: indie developers and small teams who don't have a full senior bench in-house; senior engineers who want a structured second opinion before merging; anyone who's tired of the same generic AI suggestions and wants opinionated, role-specific expertise. version 3.0.0, actively maintained at github.com/Apoorve8055/virtual-team.

plugins.name: wicked-garden
plugins.description:
Wicked Garden — AI-Native SDLC

A full software development lifecycle as a single Claude Code plugin. 14 domains, 80 specialist agents, 152 commands — covering everything from requirements through production operations.

What makes it different from a good CLAUDE.md: it's executable infrastructure, not passive guidance. Hooks enforce workflow gates before Claude sees your prompt. Context from memory, search, and project state is assembled automatically on
every turn. Decisions persist across sessions. Quality gates actually block progression when evidence is missing.

Works standalone with zero external dependencies. Local SQLite storage. No API keys, no cloud services, no setup beyond install.

Core systems:

- Crew — Signal-driven project workflows with 8 phases (clarify → design → build → test → review → operate), 7-dimension complexity scoring, hard-enforced quality gates, and multi-perspective consensus review for high-stakes decisions
- Smaht — Automatic context assembly on every prompt via 3-tier routing (hot/fast/slow). Surfaces relevant memories, code search results, kanban state, and crew context without you asking
- Mem — 3-tier persistent memory (working → episodic → semantic) with auto-consolidation, tag-based search, and access-frequency ranking. Decisions from month-old sessions surface when relevant
- Search — Code intelligence with symbol search, blast radius analysis, data lineage tracing, and service map discovery
- Jam — AI brainstorming with dynamic persona focus groups and multi-model council sessions using installed LLM CLIs (Codex, Gemini, Copilot)

Plus specialist agents for engineering, product, platform/DevSecOps, QE, data, delivery, agentic architecture, and on-demand personas.

plugins.name: wiki-knowledge-complier
plugins.description:
A. wiki-knowledge-compiler turns Claude Code into an AI-powered knowledge management system that:

Ingest → Compile → Link → Query → Write-back → Improve

- Queries the knowledge base with citations and writes back reusable answers.
- Maintains structural health: detects orphans, duplicates, stale pages, and broken links.
- Synthesizes cross-cutting insights with explicit confidence ratings and uncertainty markers.
- Everything is plain markdown with YAML frontmatter. No databases, no cloud services, no proprietary formats.
